sources.citation: Jayaram K, Full RJ (2016). Cockroaches traverse crevices, crawl rapidly in confined spaces, and inspire a soft, legged robot. PNAS 113(8): E950-E957.
sources.license: PNAS Open Access (PMC4776529) — scientific facts/measurements cited; zero paper figures or lab videos reused.
exact_claims_supported: Adult male Periplaneta americana (n=21, 0.76g, 12.52mm freestanding height) traverse 3.2mm gates in 288-821ms IQR across 5 stages.
Pass rate drops from 72+-5% (6.1 & 4.4mm) to 17+-3% (3.2mm) across 315 trials (~74% turn back, 9+-2% thorax-wedged).
104 confined-ceiling trials hold 58.05+-2.33 cm/s across 12, 9, 6mm before dropping 4x to 14.52+-0.98 cm/s at 4mm.
At 4mm (>80 deg sprawl), tibial spines engage substrate (~5.1x BW thrust/leg); across 638 runs, medium 40-grit floor maximizes speed.
Distributed cyclic compression peaks at 6.08+-1.61 N (~900x BW) with 76.67+-7.34 cm/s unimpaired post-test speed (P=0.49).
claims_not_supported: Indestructibility under sharp point loads or barefoot stomps without a 2mm stop.
Identical millimeter limits across all 4,500+ cockroach species or juvenile instars.
Claiming our procedural 3D render is actual high-speed camera footage or micro-CT.

paragraph_claims.bound_note: Everyday closed-door framing staged cleanly on 3.2 mm slot.
12.52 mm (~0.5 in) standing height vs 3.2 mm (~2 stacked US pennies = 3.04 mm) gate.
High-speed approach without pause before antennal sweep.
Downward head pitch and dorsal shell compression on entry.
288–821 ms IQR traversal (< 1 s) at 3.2 mm.
Frames the two core biomechanical questions answered in PMC4776529.
500 fps high-speed videography identifying 5 distinct traversal stages.
Stages 1–4: antennal probe, head wedge, slight pronotum roll, outside hind-leg shove.
Stage 5 abdomen exit; stiff chitin sclerites do not bend like rubber.
Rigid tergites shingle while soft arthrodial membranes fold ~41–57% (47% in 3.2 mm slit).
Contrasts narrow gate (legs outside) with continuous low-ceiling confinement.
15 cm confined tunnel stepped across 12, 9, 6, and 4 mm (104 trials).
Speed holds ~58.05 ± 2.33 cm/s across 12, 9, and 6 mm with constant ~61.05 ms stride.
2 mm drop from 6 mm to 4 mm cuts speed 4x to 14.52 ± 0.98 cm/s (P < 0.001) and breaks tripod gait.
Camera motivation introducing the rear transverse leg comparison.
Unconstrained 12 mm running engages distal tarsal claws and arolium/euplantulae pads.
At 4 mm, >80 deg sprawl tips distal tarsus sideways (+0.47 mm clearance); wide-arm push-up analogy.
Backward-pointing tibial spines contact floor at z = 0 mm and drive rearward without slip.
Synchronous mesothoracic oar shoves; ~38 mN/leg thrust = ~5.1x BW against dorsal+ventral friction.
Tarsus-ablated semicircular-track control confirmed tibial-spine kinetic friction (mu_f = 0.84–2.04).
Sets up intuitive viewer prediction ('rougher floor should always make it faster') tested next.
638 confined runs at 4 mm: rougher ceilings monotonically reduce speed (6.64 -> 5.63 -> 0.36 cm/s).
Floor speed peaks on medium 40-grit (5.26 cm/s) and drops on coarse 20-grit (3.69 cm/s) via belly snag (mu_g = 0.76).
Slit normal load ~300x BW (2.25 N); cyclic distributed peak ~900x BW (6.08 N over ~3 cm²), post-test speed 76.67 cm/s (P = 0.49).
Transitions from distributed shell resilience to 315 crevice-gate limit trials.
72 ± 5% pass at 6.1 & 4.4 mm vs 17 ± 3% pass (>4/5 fail) at 3.2 mm.
17% pass, ~74% antennal turn-back, 9 ± 2% thorax-wedged bottleneck for adult male Periplaneta americana.
Real-speed 1x synthesis of antennal read, shingle fold, and tibial-spine drive.
Viscoelastic arthrodial rebound (60 ± 12% slow-rate resilience) restores 12.52 mm standing posture.
Concluding synthesis contrasting myth of indestructibility with folding hinges + walking shins.
